notes: No trigger evals: a persona is a reviewer prompt that devpit hands to an agent, not a skill an agent picks.

Each case runs one persona as the appended system prompt, as card [devflow] 08 will run it, against a review packet; the baseline gets the same packet and prompt, and the packet names the schema, so the baseline already knows the format.

Iterations 1 to 3 are in history. They led to four changes: the reply is the bare JSON object (a sentence before it broke the parse); a broken written rule is shown with a PoC (the standards persona had rated one high without one); the schema lets an optional field be empty and requires a non-empty PoC only for critical and high; every finding keeps agent and persona (a 'leave out empty fields' line in iteration 3 made the personas drop them).

The spec persona ties its baseline in iteration 4: given the packet and the schema, a general reviewer reports the untested criterion and the scope creep too. The other three gain on staying on their own axis (every baseline mixed axes), and the security persona on the threat model too (the baseline named no boundary or STRIDE threat).
The standards persona's example was replaced after it turned out to describe the very rule break the eval plants; the example now uses an unrelated rule.
